description: Elastic N.V., a search artificial intelligence (AI) company, provides software platforms to run in hybrid, public or private clouds, and multi-cloud environments in the United States and international
description_full: Elastic N.V., a search artificial intelligence (AI) company, provides software platforms to run in hybrid, public or private clouds, and multi-cloud environments in the United States and internationally. It primarily offers Elasticsearch Platform, a set of software products that ingest and store data from various sources and formats, as well as performs search, analysis, and visualization on that data. The company also provides Elastic search product a distributed, real-time vector database and analytics engine and data store for all types of data, including textual, numerical, geospatial, structured, and unstructured; Kibana, a user interface, management, and configuration interface for the platforms; Search & AI, a platform with retrieval algorithms and the ability to integrate with large language models; and elastic security, a security solution that provides unified protection to prevent, detect, and respond to threats. In addition, it offers Elastic Observability, a solution that brings unified datastore, including Logs analytics to search, analyze, and visualize petabytes of structured and unstructured logs; infrastructure monitoring to gain visibility across cloud, on-premises, Kubernetes, serverless, and hosts; Application Performance Monitoring to support native production-grade; digital experience monitoring; large language models; and Elastic Cloud, a cloud-based subscription offering such as Elastic Cloud Hosted and Elastic Cloud Serverless. The company was incorporated in 2012 and is based in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

financial_summary: Elastic N.V. is a mid-cap technology business with a $9.0B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +18% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +5.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -13% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 73% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $322M in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.89× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, thin -1.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 17% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 2% operating margin trails the Technology median (7%) by 9pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.

The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 20% below the high.

The 27 covering analysts target $112 on average, 30% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 13% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.3%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
It runs a 73% gross margin and converts 19% of revenue into free cash flow, or 1% after stock compensation.
ROE of 29% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 17pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $799.4M (9% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.4, in the safe zone).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 17.6% over 3 years and 23.4% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 15%).
Free cash flow has compounded 76.8% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.25 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 20%.
Capex runs 1.7x depreciation (0.3% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 25, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 11.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 90%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (33 sales, net $420.3M sold).
It returns 3.8% a year to shareholders (3.8% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 5.5% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 3,834 employees, each generates about $454K of revenue, 1.2x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 30.4% a year.
That works out to $84K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.6M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
